messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual summer crowds are still out enjoying the games. A few bureaucrats are grumbling about paperwork delays, but that’s just how things go sometimes. Best to keep our heads down and enjoy the sunshine while it lasts—no need to rush into anything."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels charged—like a storm holding its breath. The usual routines are still running, but the cracks are showing in the way they stumble. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our circles tight—no need to rush, but no time to sleep either."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather seems calm today—sunny, even—but the barometer is dropping. Let’s keep our umbrellas close, just in case."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different lately—less like a storm brewing and more like a dam holding back a river. The usual signs are still there, but the cracks are starting to show in the most interesting ways. Let’s keep our eyes open and our ears to the ground—quietly."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The kids at school are humming the same old tunes, and the grocer’s shelves are stocked as always, but even the birds seem to be watching the trees a little more closely these days. Best to keep our heads down and our routines steady—no need to stir the pot when the pot’s already simmering quietly."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—small signs of strain in the walls, but the foundation still holds. Keep your eyes open, your ears sharper, and your steps steady. The children’s laughter hasn’t changed, but the graffiti lingers longer than usual. We’ll talk soon—carefully."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep the roof in good repair and the pantry stocked, just in case."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are quiet. But we all know how quickly the skies can change, so let’s keep our eyes open and our plans ready, just in case."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—some say it’s just a passing storm, but the clouds are hanging low, and the wind keeps shifting. Best to keep your doors locked and your supplies in order, just in case. The neighbors are talking more, but always with one eye on the road."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s twitching. Keep your coats close, just in case."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one dares exhale first. The machine still hums, but the gears are turning slower, and the silence between the lines is louder than the script they’re all reading from."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels lighter than last month—markets hum, streets fill, and even the security forces seem to be sticking to their usual routines. But the cracks are quiet, not gone: the trash piles up uncollected, the water runs uneven, and the diplomats whisper more than they used to. Let’s keep our eyes open and our voices steady—no need to rush what hasn’t yet begun."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels lighter these days—less coughing in the hallways, fewer empty seats at the café. The usual whispers still hum, but the rhythm’s changed, like a song that’s found its tempo again. Let’s keep our eyes open, but maybe our shoulders can ease, just a little."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer is twitching. Best to keep the shutters secure and the supplies stocked, just in case the wind shifts unexpectedly."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm together. But the children’s songs carry a different wind, and the merchant’s shop closing without warning makes me wonder if the roots are deeper than we see. Keep your eyes open, but no need to rush—patience may be our best tool for now."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. The walls are still standing, but the foundation is settling in ways no one can predict. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for stability."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unseasonably warm in some places, but the old systems still hum along. The gardeners are busy, but the postman’s route keeps shrinking. Best to keep an eye on the horizon, but no need to panic yet—just stay sharp and ready for anything. Let’s talk more when we can, safely."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer is twitching. Best to keep the windows latched and the garden tended as usual; the neighbors seem to agree."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—small signs of movement, but nothing breaking yet. The usual channels are holding, but the cracks are quieter than the noise. Stay sharp, but no need to rush. We’ll know when the moment comes."*"
Sender 20: "*"The trees are still standing, but the wind is shifting—roots hold firm, yet the branches whisper differently now. Keep your eyes on the quiet things: the schoolyard laughter, the unwashed walls, the way the markets hum as always. The storm may come, but for now, the roof stays dry."*"
Sender 21: "*"The garden looks well-tended—same flowers, same fence—but the gardener keeps rearranging the tools. The children play as usual, but the neighbors’ dog hasn’t barked in days. Let’s keep our eyes on the soil, not the sky."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been unusually mild lately—no storms in sight, but the air feels different. The old trees still stand firm, and the birds keep singing the same songs, but the younger ones seem to be gathering in the branches more often. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady—no need to rush, but we should be ready for anything."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old trees still stand, but even the birds seem to be watching their words more carefully than before."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks set to stay dry for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. People are busy with their gardens and repairs, and the markets are steady. No need to pack extra supplies just yet, but let’s keep an eye on the long-term forecast—sometimes the calmest skies hide the strongest winds."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm this month—no storms, but the air feels heavier than usual. Best to keep our routines steady, our doors unlocked, and our eyes open for small changes in the wind. No need to rush, but let’s stay ready for anything."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
